newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says in market for jet fighters.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says in market for jet fighters.

text.p: The Indonesian air force is looking at the possibility of buying jet fighters from France, Sweden or Russia following its cancellation of the purchase of nine U.S. F-16 planes, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.

Antara quoted air force chief of staff Air Marshal Sutria Tubagus as saying Indonesia was making a comparative study of the French Mirage-2000, the Swedish JAS-39 Grippen and the Russian Sukhoi SU-30.
"We are still making comparisons before we decide which plane to buy," he was quoted as saying following an anniversary ceremony of the air force operations command.
Indonesia earlier this month cancelled plans to purchase the nine U.S. F-16s over what it said was "unjustified criticism" in the United States Congress against Indonesia.

The Indonesia air force currently includes 11 F-16s purchased earlier and some 21 British Hawk jets in its inventory, according to the Military Balance of the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies.
